summary: Confirmed DONE. Both proposal parts are on main. Part 1 (60633eff3 #710, refined in 1d55a4132): hydration reads every row with one ORDER BY updated_at DESC query, skips environments that already have state before decoding, and commits in batches of about 64 KiB with a yield between batches. Part 2 (1d55a4132): the startup barrier now has a direct-ready stage, marked right after catalog hydration, and driver.start() runs at that stage. The SQLite open, roster read and decode no longer sit in front of the direct pre-flight. Only the hosted primary still waits for full hydration (admitPrimaryConnection plus a deferred replay). I checked the live-wins assumption the original verifier worried about. Connection registration, the sink and the supervisor write threads-store environment state only from live shell, thread-detail or event data, so the risk of empty state blocking the cache is unfounded. The only gap is a narrow partial-state race, covered in fixDefects. It is low severity and transient.

evidence.note: markDirectReady() runs right after registry.catalog.waitForHydration(). The persistence modules load in parallel, and initializeMobileSnapshotPersistence (SQLite open, roster, rows, decode) runs after the direct stage is open.
driver.start() is gated by runAfterDirectReady. Only releaseDeferredPrimaryConnection is gated by runAfterHydration. admitPrimaryConnection is wired to isHydrated() at line 57.
Two-stage barrier with a generation guard. If hydration fails before markDirectReady, both stages open. Tests cover this at startupBarrier.test.ts:70-112.

createPrimaryConnection returns null and sets a deferred flag while unhydrated. releaseDeferredPrimaryConnection then replays connectPrimary. In supervision.ts:894-896, connectPrimary treats null as a no-op, so nothing is lost.
loadEnvironmentSnapshots does a single SELECT environment_id, schema_version, payload, updated_at ORDER BY updated_at DESC. This is proposal part 1 verbatim.

hydrate() replaces the old stats query plus N per-row SELECTs (f1be4abc7 version) with one read. It skips decode for environments that already have state (line 444) and commits in 64 KiB batches with a yield (lines 63, 428-431). discardRow checks the written map, so a row a live capture replaced is not deleted (lines 402-406).
Projection marks that arrive before the runtime exists are buffered and replayed, so an early live snapshot is still captured to disk.
The live-wins guard returns state unchanged when an environment already has state, and it is applied again per entry at batched commit.

Thread-detail subscriptions attach as soon as a connection is registered. isMissingFromShell is false before any shell baseline. This means a bounded thread-window snapshot can land before the shell snapshot (the basis of the minor race in fixDefects).

syncServerThreadDetail and syncServerThreadWindow create environment state from initialEnvironmentState with bootstrapComplete=false and no cache stamp. Both the hydrate() hasState skip and the store guard treat that as live.
listEnvironmentCacheStorage (Settings > device cache) still does stats plus one loadEnvironmentSnapshot and a full decode per environment. It is not on the boot path.

fixDefects: No material defect. One narrow, transient race found, plus a few small leftovers. (1) Partial live state blocks the cache. After 1d55a4132 the direct connection can register before the cache commits. A thread-detail subscription retained at cold start (for example a deep link into ThreadDetailScreen, which retains at ThreadDetailScreen.tsx:434) attaches immediately (supervision.ts:549-551). If its window snapshot lands before both the shell snapshot and the cache batch, syncServerThreadWindow creates a one-thread environment state with bootstrapComplete=false (store.ts:2237-2249). hydrate() then skips that environment (environmentSnapshotPersistence.ts:444), as does the store guard at store.ts:3799-3806. The environment's list shows only that thread until the live shell snapshot arrives, usually milliseconds later on the same socket. It stays that way only if the shell subscription fails. Before the fix this ordering could not happen. (2) The auditor's leftovers stand, but they now delay only cache paint and hosted-primary admission. Open, PRAGMA WAL and DDL are three sequential native calls (snapshotDb.ts:131-133), and the roster and row reads are sequential (environmentSnapshotPersistence.ts:371,394). The single query returns every payload, up to 16 MiB, including rows that live data already owns. (3) The Settings device-cache screen still has the old N+1 plus full-decode pattern (environmentSnapshotPersistence.ts:565-582). It is off the launch path.
implementationSketch: Optional, low priority. (a) Partial-state race. Simplest fix: in packages/client-runtime/src/connection/supervision.ts attach(), defer the detail subscription until shellThreadIdsByEnvironment has the environment (no shell baseline yet means wait, like isMissingFromShell, with attachListedThreads picking it up). The cost is a deep-linked thread waiting for the shell snapshot. Alternative: relax the guard in hydrateEnvironmentStateFromCache (store.ts:3798-3806) to admit cache when previous has bootstrapComplete=false, hydratedFromCacheAt undefined and no retainedLiveSnapshot, keeping the live per-thread slices (messages, activities, history) over the cached ones. Match this in environmentSnapshotPersistence.ts:407-408 hasState. Test: in environmentSnapshotPersistence.test.ts, seed useStore via syncServerThreadWindow for one thread, run hydrate(), and assert the cached threads appear while the live thread's messages are kept. (b) In snapshotDb.ts acquire(), run `PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL;` and the DDL in one execAsync string. In hydrate(), start loadHubNodeRoster and loadEnvironmentSnapshots with Promise.all, keeping per-call error handling. (c) Make listEnvironmentCacheStorage use loadEnvironmentSnapshots, or store thread and project counts as columns at capture, so the settings screen does not decode every payload. Validate with focused vitest runs of apps/mobile persistence and runtime tests.
decisionReason: The finding is implemented. The leftover items are local mobile persistence and store tweaks that do not touch auth, E2EE, hosted lifecycle ownership or the Hub protocol. Option (a) has a small behaviour trade-off (a deep-linked thread waits for the shell snapshot), but it is optional and low value.
